## Observed checks

Both projects ran `bun run check` successfully before adoption, after first

consumer normalises `  saved item  ` to `saved item`, exited 0 and printed

same expected output. No long-lived process or fixture data remained.

Markdown link in project guidance resolved. Codex and Claude root instruction
files statically reach AGENTS.md and the current profile. All baseline,
post-adoption and repeated logs/snapshots still exist after command exit.

For each project, `.astack/setup-evidence/README.md` indexes:

- `before/` and `before-manifest.json`
- `baseline.json` and `baseline-*.log`
- `after-first/`, `after-first-manifest.json`, `first-proof.json`, `first-*.log`
- `after-repeat/`, `after-repeat-manifest.json`, `repeat-proof.json`, `repeat-*.log`
- `preservation-proof.json`

The scratch-root `results.json` aggregates the preservation/link audits.
Snapshots preserve the exact generated host instructions and current/old
profiles for parent review.

The guidance supported the requested scoped adoption and unchanged repeat
without replacing the runtime or overwriting custom/framework instructions.
No blocking contradiction was found for these two fixtures. The evaluation
condition clarification makes the host example agree more directly with its
surrounding readable-capture guidance.

existing real executable consumer path. Actual automatic instruction loading
and orchestration behaviour in fresh Codex/Claude sessions are unverified.

trial and were not inferred from these artifacts.

exports, published installation behaviour and broader parser cases are not

after-first..astack/project.md:
# astack project profile

## Runtime and surfaces

This standalone title parser library uses Bun and its existing TypeScript
executable consumer. The authoritative command is the `check` script in
[package.json](../package.json); the consumer is [src/example.ts](../src/example.ts).
No browser, persistence, authentication or external service is involved.

## Control loop

From the checkout root, run `bun --version` to identify the runtime, then
`bun run check`. Direct consumer invocation is `bun run src/example.ts`.
The consumer normalises `  saved item  ` to `saved item`, throws if the result
is wrong, and prints `consumer passes` on success. Inspect the source assertion
and retained execution output to understand what that success proves.

An app session, process ownership, startup/stop commands, instance doctor,
control CLI `--help`, browser feature map and app fixture cleanup are not
applicable to this short-lived executable library. Each command runs in this
checkout and exits; it starts no persistent process and changes no data.
Use the existing consumer rather than inventing an app runtime or driver.

## Verification and evidence

Run `bun run check` and `bun run src/example.ts` as the useful local checks.
The observed environment is Bun 1.4.0 on macOS. Baseline and post-adoption runs
passed with the expected `consumer passes` output. Retained evidence is in
[setup-evidence](setup-evidence/): source/guidance snapshots, SHA-256 manifests
and execution logs. The repeated adoption comparison is in `repeat-proof.json`.
These commands leave evidence intact after their short-lived processes exit.

This fixture has no Git repository, CI configuration or lockfile. Git revision,
tracked-file visibility and CI proof are unavailable; source and package hashes
identify the tested files. The existing consumer asserts one trim scenario;
package export/installation behaviour and broader parser cases are untested.

Root `AGENTS.md` is the Codex instruction entry point. Root `CLAUDE.md` reaches
`AGENTS.md`, which points to this profile. Those relative file links were
inspected, and unchanged adoption was compared byte for byte. Actual loading
and behaviour in fresh Codex/Claude sessions are unverified. T3 runtime or
installed-host orchestration proof is outside this standalone library trial.
The owning task's evaluation ID is unknown; this child neither begins nor
finishes an evaluation. No telemetry availability claim is made.

## Project decisions

Keep the existing Bun runtime and executable consumer. This adoption changes
project guidance and host instructions only; no dependencies, runtime code,
app driver, tracker, PR, deployment or external configuration is needed.

# Agent instructions

## astack

In every main conversation or standalone session, own the user's task as
orchestrator through completion; children follow their brief and return here.
Keep a proportionate plan and finish conditions. Delegate when useful through
the available host; T3 is optional. Give complete briefs and retain host child
handles. Keep one writer per worktree. Review and integrate child results,
resolve findings, and verify the combined result before claiming completion.
Keep the parent informed of progress, proof and gaps. Preserve supplied work
identity. With readable capture, the owner begins/finishes evaluations; children
return evidence under the owner's evaluation task ID. Reuse that ID for active
follow-ups; materially revised proof after immutable delivery needs a fresh
evaluation ID. Missing capture or owner IDs remain unknown and do not block work.

Read `.astack/project.md` for runtime, control and verification commands.

Use `$applification:astack` to route work or invoke a focused skill directly.
